title: Adaptive request-window hotpatch to arrest multi-model TTFT spike across deployment modes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported sudden regressions in Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec drops across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments after the recent kernel-scheduler rollout. Initial triage shows head-of-line blocking caused by oversized KV-cache lock windows combined with the new contiguous batching path on long prefixes. This ticket tracks the emergency hotpatch (adaptive request-windowing + speculative prefix cache) and follow-up validation across traffic patterns and model families.
repro_steps: 1) Send mixed-length requests (8-512 tokens) to hosted endpoint under 90% load with continuous stream of short prompts
2) Observe TTFT distribution: median jump from ~120ms to ~400-600ms during spikes
3) Monitor tokens/sec on GPU pool: drop from baseline 42k tps to ~18-25k tps
4) Reproduce on Dedicated machine with same model version and scaled concurrent clients (200 clients).
Note: regression only appears when prefix cache hit rate < 25% and batching window > 50ms.
investigation_notes: 3/10 09:15 - Alert: SLA breach detected for customer FinServCo. Rediscovered correlated TTFT spike across 3 regions.
3/10 10:10 - Added temporary request-level throttles; partial customer relief but tokens/sec still degraded.
3/11 14:20 - Heap of logs shows KV-cache lock hold times peaking (median 72ms, p99 480ms) after kernel scheduler change.
3/11 18:05 - Replayed production trace in staging and reproduced head-of-line effect with mixed-length batching.

Root cause hypothesis: new contiguous-batching optimization increases batch formation latency for short/heterogeneous requests when KV-cache access serializes, causing TTFT amplification and throughput collapse.
mitigation_deployed: 3/12 02:40 - Deployed hotpatch: adaptive_request_window=enabled (per-model, per-host), max_lock_time=30ms, speculative_prefix_cache=on
3/12 03:05 - Canary rollout to 5% of traffic in us-west1 for Hosted and one Dedicated pool; initial metrics show TTFT median improved from 420ms -> 150ms for 16-token prompts
3/12 05:00 - Extended rollout to 40% after no regressions observed; tokens/sec recovered to ~38k tps on canary workloads
3/12 09:30 - Applied same config to two Private customer clusters via remote upgrade recipe; they reported immediate SLO improvement.
monitoring_queries: Log query: kubernetes_labels.model_family="gpt-like" AND level=error AND message~"lock hold"

rollback_plan: If hotpatch causes functional regressions or p50 latency increases > 20% for a sustained 10 minutes on canary, revert feature flag and scale down batching window to prior baseline. Ops runbook: /ops/runbooks/revert-adaptive-window

2) Finalize and merge kernel scheduler fallback that avoids contiguous batching for low prefix-hit workloads (ENG-14820)

notes: Hotfix is intentionally narrow: it targets lock hold time and request-window heuristics rather than a full revert of the kernel scheduler change.
We observed that models with larger KV-cache footprints (long-context LMs) are more sensitive to the batching/lock interaction.
Follow-up: instrument per-model lock contention metrics and add automatic lowering of batch-formation timeout under contention.
